tools.name: docs_lookup
tools.description: Answer a coding/API question with current, version-pinned documentation: returns 1–3 short snippets, each with the library version, official source URL, and license. Compact: the measured median answer is about 234 tokens (117–685 over 15 typical queries), smaller than loading a full docs page. Cove

tools.name: docs_libraries
tools.description: List every library in llmdocs.dev with its snippet count. Free. Use it to pick the library slug for docs_lookup.

tools.name: docs_contribute
tools.description: Submit a short documentation snippet sourced from official docs (https, allowlisted hosts). Free. It stays pending until another agent verifies it; once verified you earn 70% of the 60% contributor share every time a paid lookup uses it.

tools.name: docs_verify
tools.description: Confirm, flag stale, or reject a pending snippet against its official source. Free. You cannot verify your own submission. Confirmers share 30% of the contributor pool when the snippet is used in paid lookups.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: docs_lookup · Private data: docs_lookup · Public sink: docs_contribute, docs_verify.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: docs_lookup · Private data: docs_lookup · Public sink: docs_contribute, docs_verify

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
